title: 'I was there': pride in representing Black America
summary: Greer speaks of carrying the dignity of the American Negro.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I hear the cats talking about, we -- I say this, because I'm the only one in a position to speak now, because I'm one of the few-- I'm the only living original member of the band. We carried the flag, the American flag and the prestige for my people. I hear all these loudmouths talking about so and so, the black this, but we carried the flag for the American Negro all over the United States, 1933, '34 -- most of them loudmouths weren't born even now. We carried the flag, everywhere. I don't go for this colored jive. I am an

American Negro. You hear the cats say, the black this, I'm an American Negro, pal. We carried the flag and the dignity of the American, of my country all over the world. We were treated with the utmost respect. That's right. I can say -- I am proud to be a part of it, and my word, when a question come up, nobody tells me nothing. I say I was there, when you can say I was there, that eliminates all questions.

I was there, I didn't read that. I was there, baby. God is my judge, I was there. That's all I said. I was there, baby. People ask me different things, but I was there. I was a part of that. I made millions of people -- I was part of an organization that made millions of people happy.

Duke Ellington was a legend. He carried the dignity and the prestige of the colored race all over the world, respected, the dignity, so nobody -- he lived a few days, but he lived to see the more, he was a legend before he died. I'm living, I'm a living legend. That's no exaggeration.
Millions of people are my friends. I know. That's all I can say. I was there, baby. When you can say you was there, that's high-low jack and the game. You better believe it.
